title: wkedit.sh Auto-Correction Design
desc: Design spec for wkedit.sh failure detection + arg correction + retry. Based on live test results 2026-05-18.
steps: PROBLEM DIAGNOSIS (live tests 2026-05-18): wkedit.sh wraps wkappbot file edit. When bash processes args before wkappbot sees them, 5 failure classes emerge: (1) matches-multiple: --replace-all missing; (2) old_string-not-found: bash ate backslashes e.g. \ became \; (3) invalid-regex: shell expanded $1 or ate backslash in regex; (4) args-misparse: unsupported flags like --line N caused old arg to be read as file path; (5) regex-pattern-not-found: genuine no-match -- safe final failure, no retry.

CORRECTION DECISION MATRIX: matches-multiple -> SAFE +--replace-all (warn user). old-string-not-found -> SAFE --old-file tempfile retry (identical content, bypass shell). invalid-regex -> UNSAFE (content already corrupted). args-misparse -> PARTIAL (strip unknown flags, risky). regex-not-found -> FINAL FAIL no retry.
DESIGN: single-retry in _do_edit(). Capture: err=$(wkedit.exe 2>&1); rc=$?. Parse err. Apply ONE correction only. Never chain. Always print [wkedit.sh] auto-retry: reason to stderr.

SAFETY RULES: (A) --replace-all: always warn user matches were multiple. (B) --old-file retry: note if backslash detected in arg. (C) invalid-regex: print corrupted pattern. (D) Never retry silently. (E) --dry-run flag preserved on retry.

UNANSWERED (triad unavailable): (Q1) Should --replace-all retry be opt-in via env flag WKEDIT_AUTO_REPLACE_ALL=1? (Q2) Pre-check byte count of arg vs printf to detect shell corruption before first call? (Q3) On double-fail: emit both error messages for diagnosis?

IMPL SKETCH in _do_edit(): after wkedit.exe call -- if rc!=0 then case err in matches-multiple -> args+=(--replace-all); warn; retry. old-string-not-found -> write args[0] to tmpA, args[1] to tmpB; rebuild args with --old-file tmpA --new-file tmpB; retry. esac. One retry only.

FINAL DESIGN (merged Opus+Codex): _do_edit() { local has_replace_all has_old_file has_new_file (scan args). run_once() inner fn { apply existing normalization; wkedit.exe args }. stderr=mktemp. if run_once fails: case1 matches-multiple AND !has_replace_all -> run_once +--replace-all; warn user. case2 old_string-not-found AND !has_old_file AND args[0]!='--*' AND argc>=3 -> printf args[0] to tmpA; run_once --old-file tmpA args[1] args[2:]; rm tmpA. case3 invalid-regex/regex-not-found/misparse -> cat stderr; return rc (no retry). double-fail: cat original_stderr + retry_stderr; return retry_rc. WKEDIT_NO_AUTO=1 skips all retry logic. retire _do_edit_with_retry() concept -- keep single function.

implementation delegated to Codex 2026-05-18: modifying _do_edit() in wkedit.sh to add run_once() inner fn + retry logic for matches-multiple (+--replace-all) and old_string-not-found (--old-file tempfile bypass). WKEDIT_NO_AUTO=1 opt-out. Double-fail emits both errors.
